payload.name: Preserve Resolved Dates When Updating Event Memories
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing event memory with a candidate that includes a relative time phrase, resolve the phrase to an absolute date and store it in both content and world_start.
content: When applying an UPDATE or MERGE to an existing event memory using a candidate with a relative time phrase, resolve the phrase against the message/session timestamp and write the absolute date (e.g., 2023-04-24) into the memory content and world_start.
Do not copy vague wording such as 'the previous day' or 'recently' into the updated content; the stored memory must stand alone without the source message.
If the existing memory already has a world_start, overwrite it with the resolved date for the new event unless the new event is a separate occurrence.
Stop after updating the single affected memory; do not propagate the date to unrelated memories.

solves: During memory updates, agents sometimes copy relative time phrases like 'yesterday' into the stored content and fail to carry over the correctly resolved absolute date, causing the fact's date to become ambiguous or lost. This skill prevents that by requiring the resolved absolute date to replace relative wording and update world_start whenever enriching an existing event memory.
